headline: UNH boosts aid to record $40 million for incoming class
dek: Nearly all members of the University of New Hampshire's incoming class received financial aid this year as the university increased average awards amid persistent concerns about college affordability.
body: The University of New Hampshire awarded $40 million in financial aid to its incoming class this year, the largest total in the university's history, according to reporting by New Hampshire Public Radio and the Concord Monitor.

About 96% of enrolled students received aid, up from 88% last year. The average award rose to more than $16,000 from $12,400, while university officials said the increase came from changes in budgeting for merit and need-based scholarships rather than additional public funding.

The incoming class of 2030 also posted an average high school GPA of 3.7. Enrollment in UNH's Hamel Honors and Scholars College reached 322 students, a 20% increase from last year, according to the university.

The aid increase arrives as families continue to weigh the cost of higher education. UNH reported last year's in-state tuition at $19,202 and out-of-state tuition at $39,852, figures that do not include housing, food and other attendance costs.
author: NorthEast News Desk
